## General Summary

The document is a three-page research-administration packet for **“EcoLegis: Legislative Document Management & AI Summary System,”** a proposed system developed by fourth-year Bachelor of Science in Information Systems students at Bulacan Polytechnic College. It contains participant informed-consent forms and a formal request for institutional permission to conduct research. The study will assess the system’s functionality, usability, usefulness, and effectiveness, including its guidance and counseling-related features, among students and Guidance Office personnel. The materials emphasize voluntary participation, confidentiality, anonymity, the right to withdraw without penalty, and the absence of foreseeable risks.

## Page Range Breakdown

### Pages 1–2

These pages provide English and Filipino versions of the informed-consent form. They explain the study’s nature and purpose, why participants were selected, potential benefits and risks, and their right to refuse questions or end participation without explanation. Participants are assured that their answers and identities will remain confidential and anonymous. They are also informed that interviews may be recorded and that they may receive a transcript for reviewing, adding to, or removing parts of their responses. Participants may later be asked to validate the study results and suggest improvements. Each version includes fields for the respondent’s details and signature, as well as an endorsement section requiring an Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension signature before the study proceeds.

### Page 3

This page is a formal letter dated **September 25, 2026**, requesting permission to conduct research at Bulacan Polytechnic College. The fourth-year Information Systems students propose evaluating EcoLegis among enrolled students for A.Y. 2026–2027 and among Guidance Office personnel. Student evaluation is expected to occur during vacant class periods, and participants must provide written or verbal consent. The letter assures participants of privacy, confidentiality, anonymity, equal treatment, the ability to withdraw without penalty, and the absence of foreseeable risks. Research data will be preserved anonymously for possible reuse by other researchers. The request is addressed to the Guidance Office Counselor and signed by the research group members, the research adviser, and an ORE representative.
